issues.legal_issue: A person other than the borrower who claims an interest in property affected by a secured creditor’s enforcement measure may seek review of that measure before the Debt Recovery Tribunal.
material_facts: The plaintiffs claimed that land mortgaged by named family members was joint-family property in which they had an interest.
The bank took enforcement measures against the mortgaged land and sold it to an auction purchaser.
The plaintiffs challenged the sale and sought declarations of title, partition, and an injunction.
issues.conclusion: The expression “any person” in Section 17 includes persons other than the borrower who may be affected by a measure under Section 13(4), including the plaintiffs claiming an interest in the secured property; they may invoke the statutory remedy before the Debt Recovery Tribunal.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17(1) of the Securitisation Act permits any person aggrieved by a measure under Section 13(4) to apply to the Debt Recovery Tribunal, which considers whether the measure complied with the Act and its rules. The Court relied on United Bank of India v. Satyawati Tondon for the wide meaning of “any person.”

predicates.sarfaesi_measure_dispute: The dispute concerns enforcement measures taken by a secured creditor against secured property.
predicates.claimant_claims_interest_in_affected_pro: A person other than the borrower claims an interest in property affected by the enforcement measure.
predicates.claimant_is_affected_by_enforcement_meas: The secured creditor’s enforcement measure affects that person’s claimed interest.

issues.definition: When a dispute concerns a secured creditor’s enforcement measure and a non-borrower claims an affected interest in the property, that person may seek review by the tribunal.

issues.legal_issue: A civil court cannot decide a suit insofar as it concerns the legality of secured-creditor enforcement measures that the statutory tribunal is empowered to review, including where the plaintiffs claim that the secured property belongs to a joint family.
material_facts: The bank enforced security over land mortgaged by persons in whose names the property stood and sold the land after the borrowers defaulted.
The plaintiffs brought a civil suit claiming that the land was joint-family property and seeking declarations of title, partition, and an injunction against its transfer or auction.
The plaintiffs’ claims concerned the land subjected to the bank’s enforcement measures, and the asserted joint-family rights had not been established before the security interest was created.
The High Court held that the civil court had jurisdiction because the plaint raised a title claim based on joint-family ownership.
issues.conclusion: The civil court had no jurisdiction to examine the legality of the secured creditor’s enforcement measures; the High Court’s judgment was set aside and the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 13(4) and 17 of the Securitisation Act provide for enforcement measures and review of those measures by the Debt Recovery Tribunal. Under Section 34, civil courts cannot entertain suits or proceedings concerning matters that the Tribunal or Appellate Tribunal is empowered to determine, or grant injunctions concerning action taken or to be taken under the Act. Section 35 gives the Act overriding effect over inconsistent laws, including Section 9 of the CPC. The Court applied Mardia Chemicals Ltd. v. Union of India, which held that the bar extends to matters that may be taken cognizance of by the Tribunal, including action yet to be taken; it also relied on the principle that an aggrieved person may challenge Section 13(4) measures before the Tribunal or Appellate Tribunal.

predicates.civil_suit: A plaintiff has brought a suit in a civil court.
predicates.suit_concerns_secured_creditor_enforceme: The suit concerns the legality or effect of a secured creditor’s enforcement measure against secured property.
predicates.tribunal_empowered_to_review_measure: A statutory tribunal is empowered to determine whether that enforcement measure was lawful.

issues.definition: If a civil suit concerns a secured creditor’s enforcement measure and a statutory tribunal can review that measure, the civil court lacks jurisdiction over that matter.
